articles.title: Jensen Huang's next move: Wall Street floats Intel and SpaceX, but bettors are banking on a surprise second act
articles.summary: Prediction markets think Huang is likelier to start something new than to join Intel or SpaceX.
articles.body:
F. Scott Fitzgerald wrote that there are no second acts in American lives. Silicon Valley has spent 40 years proving him wrong.

Jensen Huang has been out as Nvidia's ( NVDA ) CEO for barely a week, and everyone already has a script for him. President Donald Trump, who has defended Huang from the start, would prefer a rerun. "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump said at a White House briefing Friday , adding that a smart Nvidia would accept Huang's apology and let him return.

The casting call comes in one of the worst weeks for tech stocks in years. Nvidia has lost more than $2.7 trillion in market value since its Oct. 6 record high, nearly $900 billion of it this week, as an SEC probe reportedly looks into its accounting. The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) closed in a correction Friday, and the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) lost 10% for the week.

Wall Street has its own scripts. Speculation from Mizuho cites Huang as leading Intel's ( INTC ) AI chip strategy, though no talks have been reported. Asked on X about hiring Huang, Elon Musk replied , "That would be an honor."

Musk has also said he's signing a petition to reinstate Huang at Nvidia, along with Uber founder Travis Kalanick, who staged a second act of his own after Uber pushed him out in 2017.

The people putting money on it are backing neither. On Polymarket , the top pick for Huang's next formal role is a company he starts himself, at 27%, ahead of no new job before 2028, at 24%. A return to Nvidia gets 20%, SpaceX 8%, and Intel 3%, in a small market with about $64,000 traded.

Steve Jobs lost his operating role at Apple ( AAPL ) in May 1985 and started NeXT about four months later. Apple bought NeXT 11 years after that, and Jobs came with it. Musk was pushed out as PayPal's CEO in 2000 and founded SpaceX ( SPCX ) about 18 months later, so the company floated for Huang is itself a second act.

Intel would cast Huang as Lee Iacocca. Henry Ford II fired Iacocca as president of Ford ( F ) in 1978, and within four months, he was running the struggling Chrysler, which was later rescued by federal loan guarantees. Washington has owned roughly 10% of Intel since August 2025. But Huang is still Nvidia's largest individual shareholder, with a stake worth about $102 billion at Friday's close.

Mark Hurd left HP ( HPQ ) in August 2010 after an expense-report probe tied to a personal relationship, and Oracle ( ORCL ) made him co-president a month later. Oracle stock rose about 6% the next session, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Larry Ellison had called Hurd's ouster "the worst personnel decision since the idiots on the Apple board fired Steve Jobs many years ago."

articles.title: A 10% drop for the stock market is unnerving, but it's not that unusual
articles.summary: stock market has dropped 10% from its high set last month amid concerns about the growing hurdles faced by the high-flying artificial intelligence industry.T...
articles.body:
The U.S. stock market has dropped 10% from its high set last month amid concerns about the growing hurdles faced by the high-flying artificial intelligence industry.

The fall for the S&P 500 is steep enough that Wall Street has a name for it: a "correction." Such drops have happened regularly for more than a century, and market pros often view them as potentially healthy wipeouts of overdone euphoria, which could send stock prices too high if unchecked.

But corrections are unnerving in the moment. And the larger fear always accompanying a correction is that it could be a warning sign of a coming "bear market," which is what Wall Street calls a drop of at least 20%.

Here's a look at what history shows about past corrections, and what market watchers are expecting going forward.

Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence boom drove the markets to all-time highs in October. But a confluence of events caused investors to question whether the enthusiasm is overblown and if the AI industry can deliver on the lofty expectations.

For one, investors are worried that stock prices in AI companies shot too high and that the strong demand for memory, processors and other building blocks of data centers could fizzle out if AI proves less profitable than promised.

The large sums needed to invest in technology and data centers are another concern. The industry is racing to develop more capable models and infrastructure, which requires billions of dollars, but increasingly companies are having to raise money by selling bonds to investors. Now, the Federal Reserve is expected to hike its short-term interest rate next month. That could drive up borrowing costs for AI companies, among others.

More recently, investors have grown anxious about the regulatory environment under a new Congress. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry amid a backlash against data centers. And two big states offering incentives for data centers, Texas and Georgia, elected Democratic governors who have vowed to stop new construction.

Then there's Nvidia . The company's chips power the AI industry and it also provides the cash that's helped companies across the industry to grow. The sudden downfall of Jensen Huang , its former CEO and co-founder, has punished the company's stock and been a big factor in the broader sell-off.

"Jensen Huang's departure may have been the catalyst for this sell-off, but the underlying concerns in the technology sector have been building for some time," said Karan Ramchandani, managing partner at Post Oak Group. "Investors have poured enormous amounts of capital into AI based on expectations of transformational growth, and we're now entering a period where those expectations need to translate into measurable earnings and returns."

articles.title: Defense tech VC hit a record $37.9 billion last quarter. Two investors say it looks like 2021
articles.summary: VCs poured a record $37.9 billion into defense tech last quarter. Washington Harbour’s Mina Faltas and Eclipse’s Aidan Madigan-Curtis warn that tourist money...
articles.body:
When it comes to defense tech, it's a FOMO-YOLO market, two prominent investors in the sector said onstage this week at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit.

"I'm a long-term optimist and I've been doing this for 30 years, but I see activity in the capital markets that reminds me of 2021," said Mina Faltas, founder and CEO of Washington Harbour Partners.

"There are a lot of new entrants into the space. The death of SaaS and the disruption from AI has shifted capital into areas of deep tech, space, robotics, energy, and defense," he said. "There's folks deploying capital who aren't experts in any one of those sectors. So, consequently, we can talk about a bubble."

The money has arrived fast. Venture capitalists put a record $37.9 billion into defense tech across 269 deals in the third quarter of 2026, up 117.5% from the prior quarter, according to PitchBook data cited by Fortune in its coverage of defense tech CEOs at the forum . Valuations have climbed with it: Early-stage defense startups have fetched 17 to 50 times revenue, Fortune reported this summer .

Even the sector's biggest winners are uneasy. Anduril cofounder Trae Stephens told Fortune in June that mid-stage defense startups trade at multiples that are "completely disconnected from reality."

Aidan Madigan-Curtis, a partner at venture firm Eclipse, described the mood bluntly.

"There is a pretty big YOLO sentiment happening right now, essentially in physical tech investing," Madigan-Curtis said. "There are a lot of tourist investors who are excited about a person, a background, a theme… [and] maybe they're most excited about who invested in the last round and the signal that that gives, versus a hardcore underwriting of a real set of capabilities that can truly pierce into a market."

That froth now meets a broader shock. Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia CEO on Nov. 12, under pressure from the chipmaker's board, has left the startup ecosystem primed for change and possible disruption.

AI startups are most exposed, but private capital markets more broadly are in flux, including the deep-tech bets now crowding into defense.

For startups, the harder test is selling to the government. It has long been a difficult market to crack, and the Pentagon, which has used the name Department of War as a secondary title since a 2025 executive order , is among the hardest. Part of the trouble is that government isn't a monolithic customer, even if it looks like one.

"There's a misconception that the Pentagon is this all-or-nothing type of customer," said Faltas. "It's actually not. The building itself is… called the Pentagon. It's got five corners, and each of those five corners needs to be engaged with, and educated with, and listened to… That requires a very focused ground game."

This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

articles.title: We May Be Witnessing Wall Street's Biggest Bubble Burst in Real Time (and I'm Not Talking About Artificial Intelligence)
articles.summary: The stock market’s $1.5 trillion powder keg may be about to blow.
articles.body:
Since the 2022 bear market bottomed, it's been all systems go for the ageless Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI), benchmark S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), and innovation-inspired Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC). Since reaching their respective troughs, the Dow has powered higher by up to 90%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have more than doubled.

While the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out has been the primary catalyst behind Wall Street's gains, it's not the only reason stocks are higher. Historically low peak marginal corporate income tax rates have fueled record share buyback activity by S&P 500 companies. Stock-split euphoria and record-breaking initial public offerings are also intriguing retail investors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

While history has repeatedly shown that the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite rally over multiple decades, it also tells us that bull markets don't last forever. Eventually, something is going to knock Wall Street's AI-driven bull market off its pedestal -- and we may be watching that bubble burst before our very eyes right now .

While everyone's focused on the potential formation and subsequent bursting of an AI bubble, there's a $1.5 trillion bubble that looks to be bursting in real time.

The stock market's risk-taking bubble appears ready to implode

Even though past events can't concretely predict the future, history has a way of rhyming on Wall Street. In other words, historical precedent often sets the tone.

Over the last three decades, few, if any, past events, metrics, or indicators have accurately forecast the future quite like outstanding margin debt.

Margin represents the money an investor borrows, with interest, from their broker to short-sell (wager against) or purchase securities, such as stocks or exchange-traded funds (ETFs). When used to buy stocks or ETFs, margin acts as leverage -- and leverage can be risky.

On the one hand, if a stock or ETF moves in the desired direction, margin can help an investor amplify their gains. But if the security in question moves in the opposite direction, it can quickly magnify losses, on top of owing the broker interest on what's borrowed. This dynamic is what makes outstanding margin debt a crude but incredibly useful risk-measuring metric.

articles.title: 2 ETFs to Consider in a Market Where Nearly All Stocks Look Dangerous
articles.summary: Instead of trying to identify stocks to buy in a down market, consider these ETFs that help you exclude the biggest risk in the U.S. stock market right now —...
articles.body:
While I don't predict the future, I do gauge the odds.

And with each passing week, the odds of the broad stock market digging out of this current downturn any time soon become more remote. So instead of trying pointlessly to identify stocks to buy with any level of confidence, this risk manager will drop down a level.

Take a look at the Xtrackers S&P 100 Ex Top 20 ETF (XOEX) and the iShares S&P 500 Ex S&P 100 ETF (XOEF), a pair of fairly new ETFs which debuted not too long ago. What's the appeal for investors? They exclude the biggest risk in the U.S. stock market right now: mega-caps carrying too much of the weight in the S&P 500 index to be healthy.

If you own an S&P 500 index fund like (SPY) or (VOO), you do not own a diversified basket of 500 American businesses. You own a top-heavy momentum bet where a small cluster of trillion-dollar giants drives an outsized share of your returns.

For example, here are SPY's top 10 stocks (including 2 Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) tickers, for a list of 11 names total). These occupy 39% of the index's total weight, leaving about 490 stocks to account for the other 61%.

Think about that for a moment. One group averages about a 3.6% position, and the other about 0.8%. Like an army of ants, the latter crew can only do so much individually to alter the damage that the ones on top can do. Like now, for instance.

XOEF excludes not only the top 10, but the top 100. The remaining 400 stocks are not shrimps. But only one stock — CrowdStrike (CRWD) — has a market cap that exceeds $200 billion. No trillionaires here!

But wait, there's more. XOEX does similar math, but one step further. Whereas XOEF takes its portfolio from the 500 S&P stocks down to 400 by removing the top 100, XOEX takes the top 100 S&P 500 stocks and excludes the top 20 by market capitalization. That nets out to an 80-stock portfolio, whose biggest holdings are shown here.

Frankly, in a rough market like this, I consider an ETF like this relatively attractive, since there's a good chance nearly all stocks could plummet from here.

However, this is exactly the time for investors to identify ETFs that can serve one purpose now, and a related one later, in a calmer market climate.

articles.title: Apple Is Now Worth Over $5 Trillion Without Betting Big on AI Data Centers. AAPL Stock Now Trades Near Wall Street’s Targets.
articles.summary: Apple is worth more than $5 trillion after skipping the AI data-center spending race.
articles.body:
Apple (AAPL) is currently the most valuable company in the world with a market capitalization of more than $5 trillion. No other firm is worth even $4 trillion as of this writing. AAPL stock has been on a record run this year, currently up about 26% so far in 2026.

On Sept. 1, John Ternus took over from Tim Cook as CEO. I've noted before that Ternus is a lifelong hardware engineer, and his first big hire as CEO was a former hardware engineering vice president who he brought back from retirement. Investors have seemed to like the early signs of Apple shifting its focus toward hardware; AAPL stock rose on Ternus' first day as CEO and again after his first iPhone launch. Since Ternus took over, AAPL stock has climbed more than 5%.

However, the main reason shares have rallied this year may be that, while Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Meta Platforms (META), and Alphabet (GOOGL) have spent hundreds of billions of dollars on artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, Apple hasn't. Investors may now see that as a strength. As I wrote when Apple launched its 2-nanometer M6 chip, the company has instead been making a quiet bet on AI belonging on the device.

Bernstein believes the market is now pricing Apple like a high-quality consumer company, comparing it with Costco (COST) and Walmart (WMT) rather than other tech giants. A big attraction of buying Apple stock is its cash advantage. Because it has avoided massive data-center spending, the company can hand cash back to investors. In fiscal 2026, Apple returned approximately $102 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

After its record run, AAPL stock now trades near what most analysts think it is worth. The average price target of $344.69 is slightly above current levels. Apple has also warned that rising memory prices could squeeze profits. As a result, management expects gross margin to fall to 45% to 46% in the holiday quarter, down from 47.9% last quarter and below the 47% expected by analysts.

Apple's business is booming, but because AAPL stock has run so far, the company will need to keep delivering to justify the premium.

articles.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
articles.summary: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company’s AI tool Claude.
articles.body: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company’s AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem. Levent Alpöge, a member of the company’s technical staff, made the announcement Friday by way of a four-page explanation posted on his website. He said that he believes by working with Claude, he has found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. “Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line,” Alpöge wrote. “No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” Formulated in 1859, the Riemann Hypothesis centers on the distribution of prime numbers — those that are only divisible by one and themselves — as they grow towards infinity. Alpöge said his discovery came late Sunday night. He messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to ask about “my ability to announce,” as the San Francisco-based company was about to make major news with its stock market debut. A day after the company’s initial public offering — the most valuable in history — Alpöge revealed he’d solved the problem that has proved elusive for more than 150 years. Anthropic did not respond to an email from The Associated Press requesting comment on Alpöge’s claim. Alpöge released his and Claude’s proof of the Riemann Hypothesis within 17 million lines of Lean code, a programing language that allows people to program proofs of mathematical theorems. Traditionally the findings buried in that code would be published in a formal paper, said Alex Kontorovich, distinguished professor and department chair of mathematics at Rutgers University. “Usually when somebody gives you a paper, that’s also kind of code for a proof and you have to actually read the paper, follow it yourself, figure out if you believe every single line in that paper. And when you’re done, you should have a deep understanding of why something is true,” he said. He said Claude followed that code and said the proof is true. “Does that mean I understand it? Not yet. But the computer is extraordinarily picky, way pickier than I am and so if you can satisfy the computer, there’s a very, very good chance you’re going to satisfy me too,” he said. “But I have to do the work.” Hours after the announcement, the Riemann Hypothesis remained listed as unsolved on the Clay Mathematics Institute’s website. The institute had selected the hypothesis back in 2000 as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems and offered a reward of $1 million for the solution. The assessment process of whether the problem has actually been solved takes time, explained Martin Bridson, president of the institute. “This is an announcement of historic significance, which holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics,” he said in a statement. “But the journey from today’s announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult.” Alpöge said he is “presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.” He said more than 250,000 pages came out of his work with AI. In September, OpenAI said its technology was key in a similar breakthrough with Navier-Stokes, an equation that governs the flow of fluids. “Navier-Stokes fell and now the Riemann Hypothesis,” said Kontorovich. “There’s some kind of out-of-body experience where I’m looking at myself saying, ‘Yes, the Riemann Hypothesis has been solved,’ and kind of trying to comprehend what the hell these words are coming out of my mouth.” Anthropic made a blockbuster Wall Street debut this week, through which it raised a record-breaking $81 billion at a $1.5 trillion valuation. Amodei has projected an optimistic vision for AI’s future in which the technology leads to significant advancements in math and science research while simultaneously warning about the potential risks AI poses.

articles.title: What just happened to tech stocks?
articles.summary: It has gotten brutal out there in tech stock land.
articles.body:
'Tis the season… to be dreary about tech stocks.

On Thursday, Anthropic ( ANT ) stormed onto the public markets. Investors piled into the IPO. Interested bystanders digested smiling photos at Nasdaq of the brother-sister leadership duo, Dario and Daniela Amodei. The AI dream was alive and well.

But everyone missed the other story: The rest of tech was getting absolutely demolished.

The Nasdaq fell more than 2% by the close of trading on Thursday. Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ) were getting crushed. Chip stocks were bleeding. And the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) logged another ugly day.

The selling pressure extended into Friday. So much so that Nvidia fell to fourth place on the world's most valuable company list. The stock was down 23% over five days, suffering its worst week since October 2008.

What is going on? I would say it's a perfect storm.

The Democratic blue wave still has Wall Street questioning whether Washington is about to put the brakes on AI and data center construction. Lots of measured takes on the AI boom have hit my inbox post-election, trust me.

Nvidia has lost founder Jensen Huang, the face of this entire AI revolution, and the leadership fallout is shaking confidence. There is no timeline on when a permanent CEO will be announced, but interim CEO Colette Kress is not seen as the answer.

China is back at the center of the semiconductor trade, with fresh regulatory fears and a damaging short seller report targeting AMD.

Then there's the technical selling. Market-clearing events are forcing investors to raise cash.

Now throw in sticky inflation, hawkish Fed rhetoric, and the prospect of tighter financial conditions.

"What's happening in tech is more of an absolutely rational repricing, given that we have new facts," former Bridgewater Associates chief investment strategist Rebecca Patterson said on Sozzi Unleashed . "I mean, we lost the CEO of the central bank of AI, Jensen Huang. That deserves to be repriced."

"We have export controls. We have a Democrat Congress coming in that's probably going to take a harder look at things like data center construction," Patterson added. "And we know, especially with the outages and all those weird technical things in the last couple of weeks, we're probably going to have more of those happening as AI leads people to say, 'Oh my gosh, I need to patch. I need to find my vulnerabilities and fix them.' Things will break along the way. And so you have had a number of important catalysts leading to this repricing. I think the lower valuations make sense."

articles.title: Washington homeowner says Airbnb manager moved in, then signed a $1 quitclaim deed giving the house to his wife
articles.summary: Ellis Cameron lost control of his own home, which functioned as an Airbnb, when his the man he employed to manage it moved his family in and stole the deed.
articles.body:
If you own a house you don't live in, especially when it's in another state, you'll need to count on someone else to look after it. Ellis Cameron did that, but now, he says it cost him control of his own home.

Cameron lives in California but owns a house in Edgewood, Washington, in Pierce County. He hired Junior Patrick Adelbai to manage the property as a short-term Airbnb rental, according to KIRO 7 News . But Cameron told the outlet that Adelbai ended up living there himself, with his wife and their two kids. They even brought a dog.

Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 5 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one

Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP

A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change

"He's a squatter and he doesn't want to pay rent," Cameron told KIRO 7 News.

To top it all, a deed in the county's records now says the house belongs to Adelbai's wife, Karmaleen Issac. Cameron said he never sold the house to anyone, but now, he can't sell it as long as that deed exists in the county's records.

How an Airbnb deal ended with the house signed away for $1

Cameron said Adelbai changed out the locks and damaged the house. He asked Edgewood police for help, and officers told him it was a civil dispute for the courts. The whole time, Cameron was still paying the mortgage on the house.

"So he was living there for free," Cameron said.

But Adelbai is not at the house at the moment. Police said he shot at someone on the property on March 7. He was arrested, let go and then picked up again at the house a few days later. He's reportedly still in the Pierce County Jail, where he's been since late March. He faces trial on first-degree assault charges.

On March 19, a quitclaim deed Adelbai had signed was recorded at the Pierce County Auditor's Office. A quitclaim deed is a legal form that transfers whatever ownership the signer has in a property to someone else, with no guarantee that the signer owns it at all. In it, Adelbai listed himself as the owner and signed the house over to Issac for $1.

KIRO 7 reached Adelbai in jail and asked whether the deed was fraudulent.

"No, it wasn't," he said. "The property belongs to my wife."

Issac didn't respond to three requests for comment from the station.

Josh Dabling, a real estate attorney who worked on the case, didn't mince words.

articles.title: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million vehicles over Takata airbag rupture risk
articles.summary: Honda and Toyota Motor said on Friday they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — Honda and Toyota Motor said on Friday they are recalling about 1.6 million cars, trucks and SUVs over a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture. Honda and Toyota both said there were no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being recalled, and there have been no airbag inflator ruptures. The automakers will replace the airbag inflators in the recalled vehicles. There have, however, been at least 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009, an issue prompting the largest auto recall in U.S. history. All of those deaths involved airbag inflators without a drying agent. At least 20 of those deaths were in Honda vehicles. The vehicles in the current recalls have airbag inflators that contain a moisture-absorbing material — unlike the millions of vehicles recalled previously. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said analysis and inflator degradation simulation models conducted by independent testing groups allowed the automakers to act ahead of potential risks. “Honda and Toyota saw early evidence of degradation risk in certain of their vehicles and are currently conducting proactive recalls of vehicles,” NHTSA said late Friday, adding that other automakers continue to conduct inflator analysis and testing. The recall includes 810,592 older Honda cars and SUVs in the United States and 790,000 Toyota vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the United States. The Toyota recall includes 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 IS250, 2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models. The Honda recall covers some 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles. The Honda recall covers vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 states or territories known for high temperatures, humidity and large temperature fluctuations. Over the past decade, two dozen major automakers have recalled more than 100 million vehicles fitted with Takata airbag inflators worldwide, including about 67 million vehicles in the United States. Various automakers have also reported hundreds of injuries in vehicles since 2009 from Takata airbag inflators that can explode, unleashing metal shrapnel inside cars and trucks, killing or injuring drivers or other vehicle occupants. Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators within specific geographic regions. Toyota warned that degraded propellant could cause the inflator to rupture if the airbag deploys and cause serious injuries. The Honda recall applies to vehicles sold or registered in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Texas, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, the Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan), Guam and American Samoa. Toyota did not specify in which U.S. states the recall applies but said it expects the replacement inflators will be ready by early 2027.

They said it should provide meaningful market access, build on the complementary strengths of the two economies and create fresh opportunities for trade and investment.The ministers also reviewed the progress of negotiations and guided their respective teams to advance discussions constructively, the ministry said.The Indian negotiating team was led by chief negotiator Brij Mohan Mishra, while the Canadian side was headed by chief negotiator Mary-Catherine Speirs.The ministry said substantive discussions took place across various negotiating tracks during the latest round, with both sides making progress towards advancing the proposed agreement.The negotiations are guided by the shared objective of concluding the pact within the ambitious timelines envisaged by the leaders of both countries, the release added.The conclusion of the sixth round reflects the continued engagement and commitment of India and Canada to take the negotiations forward and strengthen their bilateral economic and commercial relationship, the ministry said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body:
Elon Musk said SpaceX's next direct-to-cell satellites, launching in 2027, will have 40x the bandwidth, and AT&T and Verizon may lose some revenue.

The hit looks small for now, since satellite signals struggle to reach phones indoors, but SpaceX's planned rooftop micro cell towers aim at that gap.

Wireless made 96.9% of AT&T's segment operating income in 2025, so pricing is what a fourth competitor would test.

AST SpaceMobile, the carriers' satellite partner, has the most to prove, and T-Mobile's partner could turn rival.

SpaceX ( SPCX:NASDAQ ) wants to sell phone service, and Elon Musk just said out loud what that means for AT&T ( T:NYSE ) and Verizon ( VZ:NYSE ) . It also lands on AST SpaceMobile ( ASTS:NASDAQ ) , the carriers' satellite partner, and T-Mobile ( TMUS:NASDAQ ) , which sells Starlink's direct-to-cell service as T-Satellite.

At the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov. 18, Andrew Ross Sorkin asked whether SpaceX would end up buying an American telecom company . Musk laid out his plan instead, said he doesn't expect the carriers to "go out of business or anything," then added: "maybe they'll lose some revenue here."

Today's direct-to-cell is a dead-zone product. Starlink said on Nov. 18 that its phone service is now live in Mongolia, where carrier Mobicom offers texting and a short list of apps outside cell coverage. Nobody cancels a phone plan over that.

But Musk said SpaceX starts launching its version 2 constellation next year, which will "have 40 times the bandwidth of the current direct-to-cell version one." That's down from the "more than 100 times" he claimed on X in October. It's still a big jump from a texting service.

Then he named the place satellites struggle to reach: "if you're indoors, especially if you have a metal roof, that blocks the signal from space." His fix is a micro cell tower that sits on a roof like a Starlink dish, going into production "I think, next year." It would run on the 800 MHz spectrum SpaceX agreed to buy from Grain Management. The FCC accepted that deal for review on Nov. 10 but hasn't approved it.

AT&T CEO John Stankey said on the company's third-quarter call that 40% to 45% of its Chicago traffic comes from indoors. He added that AT&T runs six to eight carriers of low-band spectrum per metro, against one for SpaceX.

articles.title: For many young people, the path to homeownership means moving in with parents
articles.summary: More than 1 in 5 of this year's first-time buyers reported living with parents, relatives, or friends immediately before buying a home, according to National...
articles.body:
As home prices and mortgage rates remain elevated, young people are trying a new tactic to accelerate their home savings: moving back in with mom and dad.

More than 1 in 5 of this year's first-time buyers reported living with parents, relatives, or friends immediately before buying a home, according to National Association of Realtors data, a level that jumped during the pandemic and has remained elevated in the years since. In the 1990s, as few as 12% of buyers had such an arrangement.

The uptick comes as a major hurdle to first-time homeownership — saving for a down payment — is getting harder. Higher home prices mean more money down, while rising rents eat into savings rates, slowing down the process. One study by the Center for Responsible Lending's Julian Bond Institute found that the time it takes a typical renter family to save for a down payment doubled from 8 to 16 years between 2019 and 2026.

The appeal of living at home is obvious: Housing costs are the single largest line item on most budgets, and parents are often happy to let their children live rent-free or at below-market rates.

"It's a great way to save up money," said Jeff Silver, a mortgage loan officer with Big Valley Mortgage in Roseville, Calif.

He counsels clients in rent-free living situations to make "pretend" mortgage payments straight into their savings accounts. In his area, where the median home lists for nearly $650,000, he rarely sees monthly home payments below $3,800. Saving that for a year would bring in over $45,000 and cover a down payment.

More young adults are living at home regardless of whether they're explicitly saving for a home. As of last year, roughly 1 in 3 adults under 35 lived with their parents, just off of all-time highs reached during the early days of the pandemic.

"I somewhat view it positively," Lawrence Yun, the NAR's chief economist, said of young people who are living at home and stockpiling cash instead of renting. "A down payment is one of the major barriers to getting into that first level."

Young adults who choose to move back home to fast-track their savings are trading away some short-term independence in hopes of a healthy long-term financial future. And for parents or relatives looking for ways to help children get a foothold into an expensive market, offering up a spare bedroom can be a powerful alternative to a direct cash gift.

Ruthie Bult, 26, and her husband moved in with her parents in New Hampshire shortly after she gave birth to their now 1-year-old son. They had hoped to stay just a few months while hunting for a home nearby, but found little available inventory and a competitive market. They've now lived with her parents for almost a year.

articles.title: Trump wants to work with Democrats on placing 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates
articles.summary: President Trump reupped his call for a 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates, saying he would be willing to work with Democrats on the issue. “I didn’t even know they said it but they’ve been trying to get that for years. I would do it,” Trump said during a phone call interview with…
articles.body:
President Trump reupped his call for a 10 percent cap on credit card interest rates, saying he would be willing to work with Democrats on the issue.

“I didn’t even know they said it but they’ve been trying to get that for years. I would do it,” Trump said during a phone call interview with Fox News’ “Saturday in America.”

“These credit card companies have made a lot and the credit card fees that they charge,” the president added. “I know some people would say it’s not free enterprise, but what’s free enterprise when you’re sitting home and you get a bill that some guy set up in an office on Park Avenue and they say let’s charge a fee that’s too high.”

The president’s comments come as Americans are grappling with rising credit card balances. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York reported last week that credit card balances increased by $22 billion in the third quarter. This is a 1.7 percent increase from the second quarter.

This year, credit card debt surpassed $1.28 trillion with balances in the third quarter being $52 billion more than what they were one year ago. The average credit card interest rate as of Nov. 4 stands at 19.71 percent, according to Bankrate .

Democrats previously have called for the capping of credit card interest rates and so has the president.

On Nov. 8, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), who is in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, said she wants to codify that cap when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress in January

“I got the bill, I’m ready to go,” Warren said on CBS News’s “ Face the Nation ” earlier this month.

Texas’ incoming Democratic senator James Talarico has mentioned capping “sky-high” credit card interest rates in his campaign , vowing to “rein in the predatory credit card companies ripping people off.”

Earlier this year in January, Trump called for the placing a one-year cap on the credit card interest rates, saying, “we will no longer let the American Public be ‘ripped off’ by Credit Card Companies that are charging Interest Rates of 20 to 30%, and even more, which festered unimpeded during the Sleepy Joe Biden Administration. AFFORDABILITY!”

articles.standfirst: Chuva acima da média afetou plantações na região de Itapetininga e reduziu oferta nos mercados. Em Ribeirão Branco, quebra na safra deve chegar a 17% neste ano.
articles.summary: O preço do quilo do tomate subiu nos mercados e feiras do interior de São Paulo nas últimas semanas, impulsionado pelo excesso de chuvas nas lavouras.
articles.body:
Preço do tomate dispara no interior de SP após excesso de chuvas — Foto: Reprodução / TV TEM

O preço do quilo do tomate subiu nos mercados e feiras do interior de São Paulo nas últimas semanas, impulsionado pelo excesso de chuvas nas lavouras. Em Sorocaba , o fruto já é encontrado por até R$ 26. Em São José do Rio Preto , o valor chega a R$ 23, enquanto em Bauru, Itapetininga e Presidente Prudente, o quilo é vendido por R$ 20.

A queda na oferta está diretamente ligada aos problemas enfrentados na região de Itapetininga, principal polo produtor do estado. Em Ribeirão Branco (SP), cidade com cerca de mil produtores e responsável por 6% de todo o tomate cultivado em São Paulo, a produtividade caiu. A previsão é que a safra deste ano seja 17% menor, não passando de 55 mil toneladas.

Segundo o produtor de tomate Denis Magalhães Machado, o excesso de chuva e o tempo fechado atrapalham o desenvolvimento da lavoura, pois impedem a planta de gerar frutos. Ele explica que a produção diminuiu até mesmo nas áreas de cultivo protegido (estufas), onde ainda é possível controlar o avanço de fungos e bactérias.

Há sete meses, Denis não consegue ampliar o plantio em sua propriedade, em Ribeirão Branco. Além do clima, a falta de mão de obra e o alto custo dos insumos prejudicaram os negócios.

Dos dois hectares da propriedade, menos da metade está em produção atualmente. O total de pés plantados caiu de 20 mil para 8 mil. Com isso, a colheita, que foi de 25 toneladas em 2025, não deve passar de 10 toneladas em 2026.

De acordo com o Departamento de Águas e Energia Elétrica do Estado de São Paulo (DAEE), choveu 500 milímetros na região entre setembro e outubro — mais que o dobro do registrado no mesmo período de 2025, reflexo dos efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño.

O volume excessivo atingiu diversos produtores paulistas e reduziu a oferta do alimento. Com menos produto disponível, o preço sobe automaticamente nas feiras e supermercados.

Um levantamento do Centro de Estudos Avançados em Economia Aplicada (Cepea) mostrou que o preço do tomate tipo salada subiu 64% no estado entre setembro e outubro, na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado. Em algumas cidades, o quilo chegou a ser vendido por R$ 30.

Apesar da alta ao consumidor, o valor extra não se transforma em lucro para o agricultor. O dinheiro é usado para cobrir os prejuízos e os custos elevados de manutenção da lavoura.

Dados da Prefeitura de Ribeirão Branco confirmam a redução na atividade. A área cultivada no município caiu 7%, passando de 810 hectares no ano passado para 750 hectares neste ano. Com menos área plantada e menor produtividade, a colheita municipal recuou de 67 mil toneladas em 2025 para 55 mil toneladas em 2026, gerando uma cadeia de prejuízos no setor.

Segundo o secretário municipal de Agricultura de Ribeirão Branco, José Roberto da Silva, a normalização da oferta e dos preços depende diretamente da melhora nas condições climáticas nos próximos meses.

A crise preocupa até os trabalhadores mais experientes do setor. O comerciante Luiz Martins, que vende insumos para produtores de tomate há 40 anos, afirma que nunca presenciou uma situação tão crítica quanto a atual.

articles.title: Nova espécie de perereca é descoberta em Minas Gerais por biólogos | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal com menos de 4 cm e mancha em “W” entre os olhos foi encontrado em riacho de Mata Atlântica e batizado em homenagem a Cataguases e ao povo cataguá.
articles.summary: Batizada de Ololygon cataguas, a nova espécie de perereca foi identificada em Minas Gerais após 10 anos de estudos sobre seu canto e DNA na Mata Atlântica.
articles.body:
Em uma área preservada de Mata Atlântica, em Cataguases, na Zona da Mata mineira, o biólogo Clodoaldo Lopes ouviu uma perereca que não soava como as outras.

A desconfiança levou a mais de uma década de pesquisa e terminou na descrição de uma nova espécie para a ciência: a Ololygon cataguas .

“Tinha uma área bem preservada, que tem um riacho dentro de uma mata. Ao começar a pesquisar, nós encontramos essa espécie de perereca. Ouvimos o canto dela e vimos que era diferente. Isso já despertou uma curiosidade”, conta.

Os primeiros exemplares foram coletados em 2013, em riachos de água limpa no distrito de Glória. Entre 10 e 15 animais foram levados para a Universidade Federal de Viçosa ( UFV ), onde biólogos analisaram dezenas de amostras.

A nova perereca é pequena. As fêmeas medem de 27,1 milímetros a 33,8 milímetros, e os machos são ainda menores, com 21,7 milímetros a 24,7 milímetros. Com a lupa, dá para ver os traços que a diferenciam das parentes próximas: o focinho arredondado e uma mancha em formato de “W” entre os olhos.

A confirmação veio da combinação entre aparência e DNA. Os pesquisadores retiraram pequenos fragmentos de músculo ou de fígado dos animais e sequenciaram o material genético, que depois foi comparado ao de espécies semelhantes.

“A gente viu que ele era diferente geneticamente e que tinha características morfológicas também. Então juntamos a genética com a morfologia”, explica o biólogo Renato Feio.

O nome é uma homenagem ao município de Cataguases e ao antigo povo indígena da região, os cataguás. O estudo foi publicado recentemente em uma revista científica internacional, e esta é a primeira vez que a espécie é descrita e catalogada.

Nova espécie de perereca é descoberta em Minas Gerais — Foto: Globo Rural

A descoberta abre caminho para novas pesquisas. Os cientistas querem entender o que a perereca come, como se comporta e o que é preciso para conservá-la. Há interesse até em possíveis usos farmacológicos.

Ainda não se sabe se a espécie está ameaçada de extinção. Para isso, os pesquisadores vão percorrer regiões próximas em busca de outras populações.

Para Clodoaldo, a descoberta reforça o tamanho da biodiversidade brasileira. O Brasil é o país com mais espécies de anfíbios do mundo. “E a gente pôs mais uma nessa lista. Não só brasileira, mineira, e da Zona da Mata. É legal colocar mais um habitante no planeta.”

articles.title: Ovelhas entre painéis solares? Entenda a tendência que une geração de energia e criação de animais | G1
articles.standfirst: Além de oferecer sombra aos animais, o modelo ajuda a controlar a vegetação, reduz custos de manutenção e cria uma nova fonte de renda. Mas adoção ainda é lenta e nem sempre funciona.
articles.summary: Além de oferecer sombra aos animais, o modelo ajuda a controlar a vegetação, reduz custos de manutenção e cria uma nova fonte de renda. Mas adoção ainda é lenta e nem sempre funciona.
articles.body:
Ovelhas pastam sob painéis solares na província de Guizhou, no sudoeste da China, como parte de uma prática cada vez mais comum de combinar a pecuária com a produção de energia solar — Foto: Tao Liang/Xinhua/picture alliance via DW

Tradicionalmente, usinas solares são lugares silenciosos, interrompidos apenas pelo leve zumbido dos inversores. Mas em uma a cada 10 fazendas solares nos Estados Unidos, um novo som ecoa pelos campos: o balido de ovelhas.

Permitir que rebanhos pastem sob painéis solares é uma dentre várias expressões do que vem sendo chamado de uma estratégia agrivoltaica em expansão. Isto é, quando culturas agrícolas ou animais compartilham espaço com infraestruturas de geração de energia renovável.

Os benefícios não se limitam aos animais, que passam a contar com mais sombra. Os painéis também podem proteger as plantações contra condições climáticas adversas e direcionar água para o solo, criando ambientes mais frescos e úmidos que, em alguns casos, aumentam a produtividade agrícola.

E até os próprios painéis solares tendem a se beneficiar da convivência. Quanto mais frios eles permanecem, mais eletricidade conseguem produzir por unidade de luz solar recebida.

"Se houver concreto ou algo semelhante sob os painéis solares, a eficiência será menor do que quando há plantas realizando transpiração e resfriando a superfície do solo", explicou Carl Bernacchi, professor de biologia vegetal e ciências agrícolas da Universidade de Illinois em Urbana-Champaign, nos EUA, à DW.

Embora o potencial seja enorme, especialmente à medida que as mudanças climáticas impõem maiores níveis de estresse térmico à agricultura, a prática ainda está nos estágios iniciais.

Na Europa, se a agrivoltaica fosse implementada em apenas 1% das terras agrícolas disponíveis, o continente poderia superar suas metas de energia solar para 2030.

Mesmo assim, a adoção tem avançado lentamente. Em meados de 2025, a agrivoltaica representava apenas 18,4 gigawatts de capacidade instalada em todo o mundo, menos de 1% da capacidade solar global.

A ideia da agrivoltaica remonta a 1981, quando dois cientistas alemães publicaram um artigo intitulado "Batatas sob o coletor" (Kartoffeln unter dem Kollektor). Mas o primeiro projeto-piloto só começou em 2004, no Japão, país com escassez de terras disponíveis e preocupado em equilibrar a expansão da energia solar com a preservação de áreas agrícolas.

Existem três principais modelos de agrivoltaica: horizontal, em que os painéis ficam voltados para o céu; vertical, em que eles são instalados em grandes fileiras perpendiculares ao solo; e integrada, geralmente instalada sobre estufas agrícolas.

Pesquisas indicam que culturas tolerantes à sombra tendem a se beneficiar. Entre elas estão frutas vermelhas, uvas e tomates, cujas estruturas de aço dos painéis frequentemente funcionam também como suportes para as plantas, além de pêssegos e pimentões.

Os painéis podem ainda reduzir a evaporação da água, criando um microclima mais úmido e favorável ao solo. Por outro lado, o aumento da umidade pode favorecer o surgimento de doenças em algumas culturas.

As ovelhas também demonstraram ser parceiras ideais nesse tipo de sistema. Comparadas a bovinos ou cabras, elas são geralmente mais fáceis de manejar em áreas com infraestrutura solar, têm menor probabilidade de danificar equipamentos e possuem porte adequado para circular sob os painéis.

Há ainda outras vantagens ambientais. Os dejetos dos animais fertilizam naturalmente o solo, enquanto a necessidade de herbicidas diminui.

"Se olharmos para a indústria ovina, isso representou uma verdadeira mudança de paradigma. Em vez de pagar pelo arrendamento de terras para o pastoreio, os produtores agora recebem para manter seus rebanhos nessas áreas", afirmou Austin Kinzer, especialista em agrivoltaica da organização de conservação American Farmland Trust.

"Isso altera completamente a lógica econômica e cria uma enorme oportunidade para o setor ovino, que enfrenta dificuldades nos Estados Unidos praticamente desde a Segunda Guerra Mundial."

A agrivoltaica ocupa uma posição rara na agenda climática ao combinar dois objetivos normalmente tratados separadamente: mitigação das mudanças climáticas, por meio da redução de emissões de gases de efeito estufa, e adaptação ao aquecimento global.

"Ela faz as duas coisas ao mesmo tempo, o que é bastante incomum entre as soluções climáticas", acrescenta Kinzer.

A prática oferece uma resposta para uma questão cada vez mais relevante: onde instalar painéis solares de forma eficiente sem competir diretamente com a produção de alimentos. Ao mesmo tempo, pode favorecer culturas que sofrem com temperaturas extremas ou eventos climáticos cada vez mais imprevisíveis.

Pesquisadores escreveram na revista científica Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) que as mudanças climáticas tendem a ampliar as áreas secas do planeta, "expandindo as regiões em que a agrivoltaica pode reduzir perdas de produtividade agrícola, ou até aumentá-la, além de melhorar a rentabilidade geral".

A combinação entre produção agrícola e geração de energia cria uma fonte adicional de renda para agricultores. Isso pode funcionar como uma espécie de seguro econômico em anos de perdas provocadas por secas, ondas de calor ou outras condições climáticas extremas.

"Poder contar com uma fonte alternativa de renda é algo enorme para pessoas que dependem do clima para sobreviver e que enfrentam condições cada vez mais extremas e variáveis", aponta Kinzer.

Mas a agrivoltaica não funciona igualmente bem em todos os lugares. No oeste árido dos Estados Unidos, onde o estresse térmico e a escassez de água ameaçam as lavouras, a produtividade se manteve estável ou até aumentou sob os painéis.

Já no Centro-Oeste americano, mais úmido, o sombreamento reduziu a fotossíntese e provocou quedas de produtividade em culturas como milho e soja.

Para produtos agrícolas com margens de lucro reduzidas, mesmo pequenas perdas de rendimento podem tornar o modelo inviável.

O custo também representa um obstáculo. Para os produtores de energia solar, elevar os painéis para permitir atividades agrícolas abaixo deles exige mais aço, mais mão de obra e investimentos maiores.

Os agricultores, por sua vez, podem precisar adquirir novos equipamentos ou alterar métodos de produção para se adaptarem ao novo sistema.

"Os agricultores querem aprender com outros agricultores", observou Kinzer. "Eles querem conversar com pessoas que já fazem isso."

Segundo ele, existe um problema semelhante ao dilema do ovo e da galinha. "Na maioria dos casos, eles não podem simplesmente atravessar a rua ou visitar o município vizinho para conhecer um projeto parecido e conversar com quem já o implementou."

A necessidade de grandes áreas para a instalação de usinas solares tornou a expansão da energia fotovoltaica controversa em algumas comunidades rurais.

Associações de produtores agrícolas argumentam que a conversão de terras cultiváveis em campos de painéis solares transforma agricultores em produtores de energia.

"A agrivoltaica se apresenta justamente como um meio-termo. É possível continuar cultivando a terra e, ao mesmo tempo, produzir eletricidade na mesma área", avalia Bernacchi.

Uma pesquisa apontou que mais de 80% dos americanos demonstram maior apoio a projetos solares quando eles permitem a produção simultânea de alimentos e energia, índice cerca de 10 pontos percentuais superior ao apoio à energia solar em geral.

articles.title: Empty Vande Bharat Express travels 463 kilometres with faulty brakes after railway staff ignore loco pilots’ warnings; South Eastern Railway orders probe into safety lapses
articles.summary: An empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh in October despite concerns that its braking system was not functioning
articles.body: An empty Vande Bharat train travelled 463 km from Jharkhand to Uttar Pradesh in October despite concerns that its braking system was not functioning effectively. The incident has prompted the South Eastern Railway (SER) zone to order an investigation, as the movement of a train with inadequate braking posed a possible safety risk to other passenger services.The incident occurred on October 24, just days before the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed in Assam on November 11 in circumstances involving allegedly similar negligence, according to a PTI report.Vande Bharat with faulty brakes runs emptyThe rake, comprising empty Vande Bharat chair cars, was scheduled to be hauled by a goods locomotive from Hatia in Jharkhand to Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh.According to railway officials, the braking arrangement of the passenger train had to be connected to the braking system of the freight locomotive assigned to pull it for the entire journey. However, railway personnel allegedly failed to ensure that the two systems were properly integrated. They also reportedly proceeded with the movement despite the train crew raising concerns about the braking performance.Highlighting the seriousness of the lapse, the railway zone said, "Running a train without adequate brake power is a serious safety concern that may lead to a major accident, endangering the lives of staff and passengers and affecting the safety of railway operations,"The SER zone subsequently issued an official order asking the Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) of Ranchi to investigate the matter. The order stated that instructions had been issued on October 24 for the empty Vande Bharat rake to be transferred from Hatia to Jhansi.The document, dated November 7, recorded that the locomotive pilot had carried out the prescribed brake feel and brake power test after the train departed from Hatia. The check was conducted on the Hatia-Ranchi section, in keeping with the instructions then in force.The order stated, "As per the statement of the loco pilot, the brake feel and brake power test was conducted after departure from HTE (Hatia) in the HTE-RNC (Hatia-Ranchi) section, in accordance with the existing instructions in force,"However, the test reportedly revealed a serious problem with the train's ability to brake effectively. The order added, "However, during the test, the LP found that the brake power of the train was very poor and ineffective."When the train reached Ranchi station, the locomotive pilot formally reported the problem in writing to railway personnel, including the section controller and traction loco controller. His complaint specifically raised concerns about the inadequate braking power.Despite the warning, the rake was allowed to continue towards its destination without the reported problem being resolved. The railway zone's order noted, "The train was permitted to proceed in the same condition despite the reported poor brake power,"The railway zone’s order recorded that the problem persisted even after another locomotive pilot took charge of the train at Muri station. He, too, alerted the relevant controllers about the ineffective brakes, specifically pointing out that releasing the BP pressure did not activate them.Despite warnings from the train crew along the route, the issue was not addressed until the rake reached Deen Dayal Upadhyaya (DDU) station in Uttar Pradesh’s Chandauli district. Railway personnel at DDU then examined the train and discovered that the braking systems across all its coaches had been isolated, leaving the coaches without functioning brakes.The preliminary investigation attributed the incident to lapses involving several categories of railway personnel. These included coach and wagon (C&W) maintenance staff, section controllers and traction controllers at the stations concerned, as well as the crew responsible for operating the rake between Hatia and DDU.The inquiry specifically questioned the failure of C&W personnel to carry out a physical inspection of the braking systems before the empty rake was cleared for departure. Checking the condition and functioning of the train’s equipment was part of their maintenance responsibilities, the order noted according to the PTI report.It further pointed out that railway staff did not respond appropriately even after being informed that the train’s braking power was inadequate. The order also identified a gap in the train crew’s familiarity with Vande Bharat’s braking arrangement. Because they were unfamiliar with the system, the crew did not physically verify whether the brakes in the individual coaches were engaging.Summing up the findings, the order stated, "From the above, it is evident that there were multiple failures on the part of various staff, resulting in the train being worked without effective train brakes,"The document said the rake covered approximately 463 km without its coaches’ braking systems being used. During the journey, the train relied exclusively on the locomotive’s brakes and regenerative braking.Calling for a detailed examination of the incident, the railway zone concluded, "In view of the above, it is requested that the matter should be investigated in detail to ascertain the lapses on the part of the staff concerned. articles.title: Gold falls 4.49% to Rs 1.21 lakh, silver plunges 6.6% in a single day to Rs 1.47 lakh; wedding shoppers get a buying opportunity, with some families advancing jewellery purchases while others wait for further price cuts
articles.summary: Gold and silver prices saw a steep decline on Friday, falling by as much as 6.6% as a firm US dollar, high bond yields and expectations of tighter
articles.body: Gold and silver prices saw a steep decline on Friday, falling by as much as 6.6% as a firm US dollar, high bond yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve dampened investor sentiment.On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold futures dropped as much as 4.49%, or Rs 5,733, to Rs 1,21,719 per 10 grams from the previous close of Rs 1,27,452 per 10 grams. Silver futures faced even heavier selling, declining 6.6%, or Rs 10,416, to Rs 1,47,066 per kg.The sharp correction in the two precious metals also affected gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Nippon India ETF Gold BeES, ICICI Prudential Gold ETF and Quantum Gold ETF were among the funds that lost up to 5%, touching their respective 52-week lows during the session. Silver ETFs also came under significant pressure. Nippon India Silver ETF, ICICI Prudential Silver ETF and Mirae Asset Silver ETF were among those that declined by as much as 6%, hitting fresh 52-week lows.Gold Price Crash Brings Cheer To Wedding Households But, for households that had postponed jewellery purchases because of elevated prices, the correction offers an opportunity to reassess their budgets and bring forward planned purchases!Cheaper gold can substantially reduce the overall cost of jewellery, particularly for buyers planning to purchase heavier bridal sets, necklaces and bangles. While some consumers are waiting to see whether prices decline further, others have begun placing orders to take advantage of the lower rates.At EKARAA Jewellery, the fall in precious metal prices has prompted different reactions among customers. Mehul Jain, the company's founder, told ET that the savings were less significant for smaller ornaments but became more substantial for expensive, heavier pieces.“While smaller jewellery pieces have not seen a significant impact on overall budgets, the difference is more noticeable in heavier, high-value pieces, where even a slight change in metal prices can translate into considerable savings,” he was quoted as saying.Jain said some buyers were holding off on purchases in the hope of a further decline in prices. Others, however, were using the opportunity to select designs, discuss customisation requirements and plan wedding-related orders. The response indicates that changing gold prices are affecting not only the timing of jewellery purchases but also the way customers plan them.Zen Diamond India has also seen the benefit of softer gold prices, which have added momentum to an already strong sales trend. “Lower gold prices are certainly an incentive for consumers to advance their purchases, particularly with the wedding season approaching,” said Neil Sonawala, managing director of Zen Diamond India. “We expect this to translate into stronger demand in the coming weeks, especially among customers who have already planned their jewellery purchases.”Yash Kataria, CEO of Kataria Jewellers, said the price decline had offered welcome relief to families preparing for weddings in the coming months. Even a modest reduction can make a difference when households need to purchase multiple jewellery pieces for the bride and other family members.According to Kataria, customers who had delayed buying in anticipation of lower prices were now reconsidering their plans. He suggested that families with weddings approaching should make purchases based on their actual requirements and budgets instead of waiting indefinitely for another price correction.Meanwhile, minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, released on Wednesday, indicated that nearly all policymakers believed interest rates would need to rise further to bring inflation under control.The prospect of tighter monetary policy has pushed bond yields higher and strengthened the US dollar, reducing the appeal of gold and silver to investors. articles.title: Netflix Falls Below $60. Bill Ackman Explains Why That’s an Incredible Investment Opportunity.
articles.summary: A lower share price in the short term could be great in the long run.
articles.body:
Netflix 's (NASDAQ:NFLX) share price has been cut in half from the all-time high it reached last summer. The stock now trades below $60 per share, as of this writing.

While there are reasons for the huge drop in Netflix, including slowing revenue growth and concerns about engagement, the drop prompted billionaire investor Bill Ackman to add the stock back to Pershing Square 's (NYSE:PS) portfolio earlier this year. The stock has continued to drop, though, but Ackman doesn't see that as a concern. In fact, he sees it as an incredible opportunity for investors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Netflix isn't the high-growth business it once was. For years, the streaming service burned cash to buy and produce new content and attract as many subscribers as possible. It now has over 325 million global subscribers, and adding more is becoming increasingly difficult. Keeping its churn rate low can be just as valuable as pushing for additional subscriber growth, if not more so.

To be sure, Netflix's revenue growth has slowed considerably this year. Revenue grew between 15.9% and 17.6% in the four quarters through the first quarter of this year. That rate slowed to 13.4% in the second quarter and 11.8% in the third quarter. Management forecasts just 11.5% growth in the fourth quarter.

Management wasn't afraid to touch on the reasons for the slowdown. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos said the U.S. is "just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we'd like," during the company's third-quarter earnings call. The advertising business has also been weaker than expected. "We are currently a bit behind our aggressive target for the year," Co-CEO Greg Peters said on the call. And that stems from disappointing engagement. "We want to grow view hours faster. We're not satisfied. We're working on it," CFO Spencer Neumann said.

The key detail investors could be overlooking

But investors may be overlooking a key detail about Netflix's business that hasn't changed even as revenue growth slows. Management is highly effective at dialing in content spend and reaching its target operating margin. Operating margin is on track to reach 31.5% this year, up from 29.5% last year.

What's more, Netflix's free cash flow conversion is very high and growing. It generated $9.5 billion of free cash flow through the first three quarters of the year. Netflix uses that cash to buy back shares, which supports significant improvements in its earnings per share.

articles.title: In China’s tech mecca, Trump and Xi touted AI cooperation. Now comes the harsh reality
articles.summary: Neither Xi or Trump was keen to dredge up the Nvidia scandal threatening a delicate detente between the world’s two largest economies.
articles.body: For Chinese leader Xi Jinping, hosting US President Donald Trump in the futuristic city of Shenzhen was a chance to show just how far the nation’s high-tech industry has come. But neither Trump nor Xi seemed keen to address an unpleasant reality – that the US had just announced fresh efforts to keep it from advancing much further, amid allegations a Chinese intelligence operation had targeted the head of Nvidia, one of America’s most important tech companies. The two heads of state met for the third time this year during an annual gathering of economic leaders from the Asia-Pacific region. Like the last two times, the meeting itself was a sign of reassurance for what has become a bitter and bruising rivalry. Amid all the grand gestures, including a historic meeting between the leaders of the US, China and Russia, neither side was willing to dredge up the scandal threatening a delicate detente between the world’s two largest economies. Allegations that Jensen Huang, who until recently helmed the $4 trillion chip titan Nvidia, was having an affair with a woman suspected of working with Chinese intelligence, have reignited fears of America’s best technology falling into adversarial hands. Then, two days before Trump landed in Shenzhen, the Commerce Department issued new licensing requirements aimed at further cutting off Chinese access to advanced US chips. “With the fallout of Nvidia and these new export control rules landing just before the summit, I think the uneasy truce between the US and China is even more fragile,” said Benjamin Kostrzewa, an international trade law expert and Hong Kong-based partner at the law firm Hogan Lovells Cadwalader. In a carefully orchestrated week of events for corporate executives and global delegates, Xi’s priority was to portray China as a reliable and innovative economic partner that welcomed foreign businesses. But analysts said America’s latest chip curbs, likely seen as an escalation of US protectionist policies, would be hard for Beijing to ignore much longer. China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the new restrictions “a typical case of economic coercion.” The day before Xi greeted Trump warmly at the foot of Air Force One, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce warned: “If the US insists on this direction, China will take countermeasures and firmly safeguard its national sovereignty, security and development interests.” Trade truce at risk A tentative economic ceasefire between the US and China was already on shaky ground. When Trump and Xi last convened in Washington, DC in September, they extended a trade agreement from October 2025, which included a rollback of US tariffs in exchange for Chinese commitments to buy more US agricultural products and loosen restrictions on rare earth exports. Officials said the two-month extension, set to expire January 10, would allow them to assess whether China could alleviate US concerns that it was coming up short on its original pledges. Now the controversy over Nvidia – and how some of its most advanced chips reach China despite US export controls – has triggered greater suspicion over national security risks that will complicate negotiations, said Jyh-An Lee, law professor and executive director of the Centre for Legal Innovation and Digital Society at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. “The political climate is now quite different,” Lee said. “It’s not that easy to go back to the time before the Jensen Huang incident.” At the summit, the US, China and Russia said they discussed the need to develop artificial intelligence safely. Otherwise, there was little concrete progress on trade or technological cooperation. In a Wednesday interview with Fox News, Trump said he raised Huang briefly with Xi, only to lament the “tragedy” of the Nvidia co-founder stepping down. Chinese officials have decried allegations that Beijing was using Huang’s affair to obtain sensitive information as baseless attempts to smear China. Semiconductors have become a major flashpoint in the US-China relationship, as each nation has invested heavily in surpassing the other in AI and advanced technological capabilities. While China has made it a national priority to be able to develop its own semiconductors, many of its tech companies still use American chips. That fierce rivalry will make it hard for the two nations to collaborate on sensitive sectors like technology, even as leaders tout dialogue on AI safety. And Huang’s resignation means the loss of one of the most vocal advocates for selling more US chips to China. “The US has been trying to find more bargaining chips, and I think chips might be the most valuable asset that US still has the advantage over,” said Lee. ‘One final chance’ As the host of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, it was in Xi’s best interest to maintain an image of openness and collaboration during the summit. “Simply the optics of China hosting APEC puts him in a really powerful position, so in many ways he comes out as a winner,” said Han Lin, China country director for The Asia Group, a business consulting firm. “That said, China has to retaliate. They have no choice.” Still, Lin said China would likely take subtle actions to try and preserve stability ahead of the politically important Communist Party Congress next year, at which Xi is expected to claim another five-year term as leader. One of the most effective countermeasures at China’s disposal is its near-monopoly on rare earths and other minerals critical to many high-tech supply chains. Despite the trade agreement reached last year, Chinese rare earth exports to the US remain about 75% below pre-restriction levels, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies. “China can hit back, and they can hit back hard,” said Lin. “They still continue to have the critical earth minerals export control leverage, and that really is the leverage for all seasons.” Analysts said as US lawmakers increase scrutiny over tech exports to China, that will likely lead to stronger enforcement of existing regulations, as well as new rules. Trump and Xi are set to meet once more this year, at the G20 Leaders’ Summit in December. But in January, Democrats will take control of the House and Senate after their sweeping midterm election victory, which could put pressure on Trump in his dealings with Xi. Holding the majority would allow opponents to push back on Trump’s more aggressive protectionist policies, giving China more leverage to negotiate next year. But Democrats have also called for stronger tech export controls in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, and voiced concerns about the threat that Chinese tech poses to US national security. “The takeaway we’ve been telling our US clients has been, if you have any ask of the Chinese government, better you ask sooner than later,” Lin said. “You have one final chance in G20. After which, well, we’re going to be playing a different game going forward.”

articles.title: Tesla Just Started Selling Cybercabs, Here's What It Means for a SpaceX and Tesla Merger .
articles.summary: Only a hefty cash premium is likely to satisfy most Tesla investors in the event of a merger, and that premium is likely to rise with a successful robotaxi r...
articles.body:
The news that Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA)is inviting select customers to buy Cybercabs isn't a game changer from a financial perspective (at least not immediately). Still, it is highly symbolic and highlights the case for Tesla shareholders holding fire on agreeing to a potential merger with Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) (or SpaceX for short). Here's why.

In itself, buying a Cybercab right now is hardly an attractive option for most people. They are reported to cost $29,990, but they can't be used without a $299 monthly subscription, they lack manual driving controls (a steering wheel, pedals, etc.), and they can only operate in the limited geo-fenced areas where the robotaxi service currently operates.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

However, they will obviously attract Tesla enthusiasts, social media influencers, and those confident in widespread regulatory approvals for Tesla's robotaxi service. To be clear, as management is, it's focused on becoming a transportation-as-a-service company with the "vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and Transport-as-a-Service," according to CEO Elon Musk.

The reality is their sale is more about generating promotional buzz around robotaxis as the company prepares for a widespread expansion in 2027. Fortunately, everything points to a quantum leap in the robotaxi rollout next year. The company continues to develop its next major upgrade of its full self-driving software, namely v15, which should be validated and released by early 2027 .

Also, Cybercab production is ramping up, and Tesla says it's gathering data on unsupervised miles with its robotaxi at a double-digit weekly growth rate.

What it means for a SpaceX and Tesla merger

After years of delays and missed timelines, everything points to Tesla finally releasing value from its robotaxi service next year. At which point, its investors are entitled to ask whether it would make sense to agree to a merger with SpaceX before the robotaxi ramps up.

While an offer is not on the table, and investors don't know the terms of a deal, or whether there will even be one, it's hard not to think that a robotaxi ramp-up in 2027 would increase Tesla's share price.

articles.body:
Grant Cardone's inflation math holds up: $1 million in 1960 equals about $11 million today, but his $10 million "rich" threshold overstates what most retirees need.

At the 4% rule, $1 million pays about $40,000 a year, roughly half of average household spending of about $82,000.

Your rich number is 25 times the spending gap left after Social Security and pensions, which puts most retirees far below $10 million.

Picture a 62-year-old couple who just crossed $1 million in retirement savings after three decades of regular 401(k) contributions. Real estate investor Grant Cardone would tell them they're broke.

Cardone posted a TikTok video in 2024 with a title that opens with "If You're A Millionaire You're Broke" and ends with "Get To $10 Million To Be Considered Rich." Both reactions carry a cost. Accept his number and you might work years longer than you need to, or take on extra investment risk chasing a target you don't need. Wave him off completely and you can underestimate how hard inflation hits a fixed balance.

Our view: Cardone's inflation math is correct, and his conclusion is wrong for most retirees. Whether $1 million is enough depends on one figure he never talks about.

Cardone's 1960 Inflation Math Checks Out

Cardone said, "A million was a lot of money in 1960. If money deflated at the rate that it has in my 65 years, money is worth 10% of what it was then."

The Consumer Price Index backs him up. It stood at 29.6 in 1960 and 338 in October 2026. That makes $1 million from 1960 worth about $11.4 million in today's dollars. If you want the status a 1960 millionaire had, his $10 million figure is roughly right.
