In the Fed's distributional data, a household needed $240,508 to reach the top half and $2,135,868 to reach the top 10% (cutoffs measured in 2022). A $1 million household lands between those two lines. That's comfortably upper-middle, a long way from broke.

articles.title: The Great Cash Grab Is Crashing Gold, Silver And Bitcoin, Goldman Sachs Warns The Stock Selloff Isn't Over
articles.summary: The CME Group's FedWatch tool showed traders are pricing in an 88.6% chance of a Fed rate hike at its upcoming December meeting, making liquidity tighter.
articles.body:
Computer-driven funds could sell as much as $80.6 billion in stocks if markets continue to fall, Goldman Sachs warned.

Bitunix analysts said the simultaneous drop across traditional safe havens and crypto was due to tightening liquidity, persistent inflation, year-end cash demands and leveraged positions.

Gold dropped as much as 37% since its January high as economist Peter Schiff warned that persistent inflation could lead to more losses.

Gold, silver and Bitcoin (BTC) plunged this week as rate-hike expectations and a tech-stock rout drove investors to sell even the assets meant to protect them.

Spot gold closed down 8.71% this week at $3,543.60, down about 37% since its record high of $5,589.38 on Jan. 28. Silver also dropped even harder and is now about 65% below its January high, according to TradingView data.

Bitcoin, sometimes called "digital gold," also fell to about $55,100 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024, with market commentators like Arthur Hayes predicting a lower low of $5000 .

Goldman Sachs Warns Of $80B Stock Selling

Goldman Sachs warned that if the market keeps sliding, funds could sell up to $80.6 billion in stocks this week. Even a bounce could trigger $28.6 billion in selling, according to Bloomberg.

Goldman's Panic Index reached 9 out of 10 on Friday. The firm's trading desk expects computer-driven funds to continue selling shares next week, even if the market rallies. Goldman estimates the funds sold $57 billion in equities over the last month and hold a net short position of $19 billion in U.S. stocks.

Analysts at crypto exchange Bitunix said the joint slide is a sign of tight funding and cash requirements, not a weakness in any asset. Sticky U.S. inflation has boosted rate-hike bets, pushing up the dollar and Treasury yields, the analysts added. Selling in AI stocks and the need for cash at year-end have also weighed.

Markets are "prioritizing liquidity needs and leverage management over simply seeking defensive assets," the analysts wrote. They added that "in the short term, a break below $61,250 could expose BTC to further tests of $60,600 and $60,000. Conversely, a recovery above 62,265-62,720 accompanied by improving CVD would warrant attention to a potential short squeeze."

The CME Group's FedWatch tool showed traders are pricing in an 88.6% chance of a Fed rate hike at its Dec. 8-9 meeting.

articles.title: A battered stock market looks for the bottom: What to watch this week
articles.summary: After a week headlined by the Anthropic IPO and the long-awaited release of GTA VI, the upcoming five-day stretch should be a bit calmer.
articles.body:
It'd be impossible to top last week's action. Anthropic ( ANT ) went public, marking the first pure-play generative AI lab to list on the public market in the US. GTA VI was released to near-unanimous adoration and record sales. President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral talks.

And the stock market got crushed, with the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) losing over 8%.

To put it mildly, it was a big one. Luckily for investors, the upcoming holiday-shortened Thanksgiving stretch should be a bit tamer with no key standout events. (Though, in this market, don't ever discount the possibility of a dark horse event.)

A relatively modest earnings calendar will be helmed by IT leader HPE ( HPE ) and computer giant Dell Technologies ( DELL ) on Monday and Tuesday, respectively, complemented by a smattering of retailers, including Dollar Tree ( DLTR ), Best Buy ( BBY ), Burlington Stores ( BURL ), and Dick's Sporting Goods ( DKS ).

Medical device maker Agilent Technologies ( A ) and software names Workday ( WDAY ) and Zoom Communications ( ZM ) will also share their quarterly reports.

The headline event on the economic data front will be Wednesday's monthly Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report, the core reading on which is the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation — a key data read ahead of the Fed's December meeting. Investors will also get broader reads on the economy with S&P Global's activity PMIs and the Chicago Fed's national activity index on Monday, followed by a consumer sentiment vibe check brought to you by the Conference Board on Tuesday.

Anthropic's real test begins as it starts its post-IPO journey

Anthropic finally went public on Thursday as the first public pure-play generative AI lab. The reception has been thus far — mixed, to say the least.

Anthropic made a record debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price. But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17% on the day, giving Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

Shares of the model builder dropped around 10% on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Not helping sentiment: The broader market plunged on Anthropic's well-received IPO day and remains under pressure today, a sign of a test ahead of investor appetite.

articles.title: Democrats swept Congress on high prices. Here’s how they plan to bring costs down
articles.summary: Democrats swept to control of Congress in the midterm elections due in large part to Americans’ concerns about the cost of living. Now, the pressure is on the party to deliver. On the campaign trail, Democratic leaders, lawmakers and candidates vowed to lower prices by reining in President Trump’s tariffs, forcing him to wind down…
articles.body:
Democrats swept to control of Congress in the midterm elections due in large part to Americans’ concerns about the cost of living .

Now, the pressure is on the party to deliver.

On the campaign trail, Democratic leaders, lawmakers and candidates vowed to lower prices by reining in President Trump’s tariffs, forcing him to wind down the costly Iran war , restoring expired Affordable Care Act (ACA) premium subsidies and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act .

Since the election, Democrats have doubled down on that rhetoric, pledging to tackle elevated costs once their House and Senate majorities become official in January.

“Our message to the American people who are struggling in this failed economy is a simple one: We hear you, we see you, we feel you, and House Democrats are committed to making life better for you,” House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), the likely next Speaker , said Wednesday .

Jim Kessler, the executive vice president for policy at Third Way, told The Hill that Democrats can “immediately” lower prices by restoring the ACA subsidies and clawing back the cuts Republicans made to Medicaid .

But the party should not focus solely on undoing Trump and GOP policies, he argued.

“I’d have a list of things that would … affect affordability right away, and would affect affordability long term,” added Kessler, the former policy director for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.).

One way Democrats can make an immediate economic impact, Kessler noted, is backing an increase to the federal minimum wage .

The minimum wage, which is $7.25 an hour, last increased in 2009 under legislation that a Democratic Congress passed and former President George W. Bush signed into law.

“I expect Democrats will seek to significantly increase the minimum wage. … My guess is it’ll be in the vicinity of $15 [per hour],” Kessler said.

There are 36 states and territories where the minimum wage is below $15 an hour. Kessler said that newly elected Democratic governors and state legislators should make raising their states’ standard a priority.

Jeffries backed an increase to the federal minimum wage after the midterms, saying he will discuss it with the caucus and his Senate counterparts to “see what’s possible.”

The New York Democrat told reporters, “It certainly needs to be increased. It’s a disgrace that the minimum wage hasn’t been raised in 20 years.”

Raising the minimum wage would put more money in Americans’ pockets. As far as lowering the cost of goods , Jeffries, Schumer and Democrats across the country have zeroed in on ending the Iran war and reeling in Trump’s tariffs.

The Middle Eastern conflict , in its ninth month, cost taxpayers $48.3 billion as of Nov. 13, Pentagon budget official Arthur Miller told the Senate Armed Services Committee on Thursday.

The war also put upward pressure on gas , diesel and fertilizer prices, as the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on transit in the Strait of Hormuz hindered a key global shipping route.

Forcing the president to wind down the conflict, as Senate Democrats unsuccessfully attempted to do on Thursday, could bring relief at the pump .

But experts have warned the oil industry will need months, and even years, to recover from the supply shocks — particularly the damage to Middle Eastern refineries from Iranian strikes.

To make a faster impact on prices, Democratic lawmakers should reclaim its tariff authority from the president and overturn his sweeping import taxes, argued Ed Gresser, the vice president and director for trade and global markets at the Progressive Policy Institute.

“This is a policy that has failed on its merits,” Gresser told The Hill, noting tariffs’ unpopularity among Americans.

Trump’s threat of 50 percent tariffs on Canadian autos and steel is also “pretty threatening” to the economy, Gresser said, adding Democrats should make cracking down on those levies an “urgent” priority if they go into effect. The president has said the levies will take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

Yet even before Trump returned to office, Americans had concerns about the cost of living . Three-fourths of voters told NBC News in 2024 that inflation had caused their families either “severe” or moderate hardship.

That puts the onus on Democrats to deploy their new majorities to lower costs. Sen.-elect James Talarico (D-Texas) laid out that mandate the day after he won his race, telling CNN’s Erin Burnett that Americans are “giving Democrats one last chance to deliver for them.”

How Democrats seek to deliver for Americans can take multiple forms, Kessler said. The Third Way co-founder highlighted an expanded child tax credit and permitting reform as two options for lawmakers.

Angel Padilla, the vice president for Strategy and Policy at the National Women’s Law Center, also urged Democrats to propose universal childcare .

“We expect childcare to be one of the things that Democrats lead with, and we’re actually hoping that it will be in the top slate of bills from Jeffries once they take over,” he told The Hill.

Padilla also referenced restoring the ACA subsidies , which Democrats in Congress passed in 2021 and extended in 2022 , that lapsed at the end of last year under the Republican majority.

Reversing the GOP’s reforms to Medicaid, which take full effect at the end of December and could lower spending on the program by as much as $1 trillion, would also show Democrats are doing “something to lower healthcare costs,” Padilla said.

Those two changes would return the healthcare industry to the status quo from before the second Trump administration. Progressives on Capitol Hill, meanwhile, are charging forward with their attempts to pass Medicare for All in the next Congress.

Jeffries has also proposed expanding Medicare to include coverage for dental, vision and hearing and lowering the eligibility age.

Padilla, though, acknowledged the political reality for the party. Without a two-thirds supermajority to override Trump’s potential vetoes , going “bold” on healthcare may be an uphill battle.

That makes overturning changes Republicans have made over the last two years the top priority, Padilla noted.

“People want immediate relief from the high cost of living, and the way that you provide immediate relief is to undo some of those things,” Padilla said.

articles.title: From Anthropic to Nvidia, Wall Street just had a bizarre, wild week
articles.summary: This has been a week for the ages in the investing world, no doubt.
articles.body:
I have seen a lot in the investing world over the past 20 years. Mostly good. A lot of bad.

But I have to say: This past week will live on with me until I retire.

Anthropic ( ANT ) just put a $1.2 trillion price tag on the AI dream. The AI lab opened its first trading day on Thursday at $111.50 per share — well above its $83 per share IPO price — and closed out Friday at $88. The company has dethroned Elon Musk's SpaceX ( SPCX ) as the largest IPO in history, raising $81 billion in its IPO compared to $75 billion for SpaceX.

The stock opened for trading on the Nasdaq around 11:45 a.m. ET — earlier than many thought it would — under the ticker symbol ANT. (Ants are also what Anthropic's employees call one another — true story.)

Speaking of the Nasdaq, things were pretty much locked down over there. We weren't allowed in the booth to record or go live. It's my understanding that's how Anthropic wanted it, or at least this was the prepared line.

I find it bizarre that a company trying to hype its do-gooder vibes kept media out of the building. An array of reputable media outlets broadcast from the Nasdaq each day. To keep them out on the directive of Silicon Valley elites and their PR handlers is surprising.

Tens of millions of average investors were studying Anthropic on IPO day, and this company pretty much said, "Go read the S-1 and leave us alone."

I can tell you a lot of good people were not happy about this, including a few inside the frontier AI lab. But maybe at this point in the year, nothing should surprise me!

Meanwhile, over at Nvidia, the mood is a whole lot darker .

The company that made this AI boom possible continues to face a stunning leadership crisis even as it tried to make a clean break from founder Jensen Huang on its earnings day this past week. Jensen Huang is gone. Employees are rattled.

At the first company-wide all-hands meeting without Huang on late Wednesday, interim CEO Colette Kress basically played corporate therapist by promising raises, promising more stock, and trying to keep people from walking out the door.

Oddly though, Kress didn't take any employee questions directly. I find this bizarre too, and so have others, judging by the messages I received on X. An all-hands meeting is supposed to be for employees to ask questions of leadership, not just for leadership to talk to employees.

Nonetheless, Anthropic cashed in on AI mania, while Nvidia is trying to hold its workforce together. Interesting times in investing!

articles.title: The American dream of home ownership recedes as mortgage rates surge
articles.summary: Chanell Thomas Herbert was dejected after the past year trying to buy her first home in Bridgeport, Connecticut. The houses online were "just...
articles.body:
Chanell Thomas Herbert was dejected after the past year trying to buy her first home in Bridgeport, Connecticut. The houses online were "just so beautiful" — but then "you scroll down, look at the price, look at the taxes, and it just wipes everything away".

Herbert, a 45-year-old nurse aide who is looking for a house to share with her brother, is part of a growing pool of Americans whose dream of owning a home feels out of reach as the US housing market enters a deepening freeze.

"I just want to be able to afford the mortgage . . . but it is so sky-high right now," said Herbert.

President Donald Trump pledged to lower mortgage rates to 3 per cent when he returned to the White House in 2025. Nearly two years later, the rise in Treasury yields sparked by the war in Iran has pushed up homeowners' borrowing costs as the benchmark 30-year mortgage rate surged to over 7 per cent.

Anger over the elevated prices of housing, fuel and other living costs led voters to deliver a searing rebuke to Trump's Republican Party in the recent midterm elections.

But with the protracted conflict in the Middle East fuelling higher borrowing costs, a Democratic majority in the House and Senate in January is unlikely to ease the plight of prospective homebuyers anytime soon.

Pape Ndao, a real estate broker in Fairfield County, Connecticut, who is helping Herbert with her search, said that since rates began climbing, it has been "extremely, extremely tough" finding homes for first-time homebuyers.

"Every decision made in DC affects the American dream for them," said the realtor, who works with the agency ReMax.

Across the country, Americans are being hit by higher borrowing costs.

Atlanta Federal Reserve data shows that, in February, before the US first bombed Tehran, the monthly mortgage payment on the purchase of the average home was $2,072. By August it had risen to $2,350 — excluding higher taxes and insurance costs.

House prices over the period have also risen, with the cost of the median home increasing from $382,000 to $406,000.

"The majority of the young people who are looking to buy a home are still renting or very frustrated. And that group keeps growing every year," said Barbara Denham, lead US economist at Oxford Economics.

Denham added: "Consumers know that it's really about mortgage rates. The house prices have gone up but not nearly like the mortgage rates."

The rise in mortgage rates and broader cost of living crisis have resulted in a significant market slowdown that a slew of bad housing data had augured for months.

Nvidia's SEC and CEO shocks test whether the AI factory story survives without its founder

articles.title: What a wealth tax looks in the age of AI billionaires
articles.summary: Anthropic’s initial public offering has created overnight multi-millionaires (and some billionaires), and the timing is complicated.
articles.body: Anthropic’s initial public offering has created overnight multi-millionaires (and some billionaires), and the timing is complicated. They are coming into incredible wealth just as some states are trying different forms of wealth taxes, fueled by a shrinking middle class and growing unease about the concentration of wealth and power. New York City is about to charge an extra yearly tax on expensive homes that aren’t anyone’s primary residence. Washington, DC is considering a tax on investment income for wealthier households. Washington state will levy its first modern income tax on households making more than $1 million in 2028. California’s Prop 40 “billionaire tax” failed on Election Day, but Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D- MD) told Politico that the failure of Prop 40 suggests one state can’t do it alone. A bill introduced in both the House and Senate already proposes a 5% tax on the net worth of America’s billionaires, which could become a flashpoint in the 2028 presidential election. Prop 40’s defeat — and the sudden emergence of a new class of AI elite — has simply launched a more heated national debate about how exactly the rich should be taxed. Not as much cashflow as you think “If someone’s worth $1 billion, that doesn’t mean that they have $50 million of cash around to pay the tax,” said Anderson Lafontant, managing director of Blue Zone Wealth Advisors. Lafontant, whose clients include employees of AI companies, said a lot of this net worth is mostly on paper. Companies in IPO scenarios have restrictions on when shareholders can sell stock after it goes public, so an employee may not hold much liquid cash until their shares are sold. (Lafontant does not currently work with any Anthropic employees or founders.) Prop 40 would have levied a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaires who lived in California on January 1, 2026, not counting real estate or most retirement accounts. “That’s the point about a wealth tax, is it hits paper wealth,” said Tom Steyer, billionaire climate activist and former California gubernatorial candidate. He argues that a person could borrow against stock to pay taxes. He called Prop 40 “imperfect” but “better than nothing.” Tensions with the rich Megan Lisa Jones, a private wealth and tax attorney at Holland & Knight, said some of her clients have left or talked about leaving California to seek better tax rates and avoid a potential Prop 40. Lafontant also said some of her clients have moved for tax reasons, though not necessarily over a wealth tax. Both said their high-net worth clients did not want to speak with CNN. “Some of my clients would say, ‘Well, I can’t leave now, but I’ll leave in four years…and I’m not a billionaire yet, so I don’t need to worry about it yet.’ But if they tax the billionaires, it’s just a question of time before it starts trickling down and taxes everyone,” Jones said. Steyer has said a national wealth tax would be better, so the wealthy don’t keep moving to find tax havens. “I’m not mad at people for being rich. It’s just that people are really suffering on the other end,” he said. California Governor-elect Xavier Becerra has called Prop 40 “sketchy policy” and said the state needs a long-term solution instead of a one-time affair. His spokesperson told CNN in a statement that the success of Prop 3, a state measure that made extra taxes on high-income earners permanent, is proof that California voters support taxing the rich. Beyond the Golden State Washington state voters upheld a so-called “millionaires’ tax” on Election Day, where any income over $1 million will get taxed. This means two spouses each making more than $500,000 would be taxed like millionaires. There is currently no income tax in Washington state. Pending a constitutional challenge, this tax of 9.9% goes into effect in 2028. That has prompted Michelle Dellino, a family law attorney in Seattle, to advise her clients to think through big life decisions. “Some of those choices — like marrying, signing a prenup or moving — can’t really easily be undone,” she said. Some of her clients might also be subject to a “scary” tax bill when company stock vests and is taxed like salary, even if the employee doesn’t have cash from selling those shares. What ‘rich’ really means The soaring cost of living nationwide raises questions about whether being a millionaire still holds the financial significance it once did. For example, the median single-family home in Seattle sold for about $1.1 million in October, according to an analysis by JanusGroup Real Estate. Lafontant said those who own assets in America are winners, “and if you’re not an asset owner, you are just getting gobbled up by inflation.” If a “wealth tax” is implemented she said she’d prefer to see taxes levied when people sell assets, not when they’re holding them. As AI changes society, Jones poses a broader question about the American tax policy relying heavily on ordinary income. “If we don’t have people working the same way, if AI really does replace jobs, then we’re going to have another big challenge with our tax system and how we’re going to fund things,” she said.

articles.title: Nvidia chip case: How Chinese man in Megaspeed built network serving China with Alice Huang
articles.summary: A Chinese national facing fraud charges in Singapore over the alleged diversion of Nvidia-powered servers to China played a key role in a network of
articles.body: A Chinese national facing fraud charges in Singapore over the alleged diversion of Nvidia-powered servers to China played a key role in a network of companies that supplied advanced computing capacity to Chinese customers, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal (WSJ).The 52-year-old man, identified as Li Ming, was deeply involved in the operations and major business decisions of Singapore-based Megaspeed, and also had links to other companies trading Nvidia chips, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company where Alice Huang served as managing director. The latest report follows earlier revelations linking Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive to Nvidia founder and then CEO Jensen Huang.How the alleged chip-smuggling network operatedSingapore prosecutors charged Li and others with fraud in February 2025 over the alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. While several companies were named in the case, Megaspeed was not among them, the report said.According to prosecutors, Li bought computer servers equipped with Nvidia chips and allegedly misled the American supplier by claiming the equipment was intended for his Singapore-based company, Luxuriate Your Life.The servers were allegedly shipped to neighbouring Malaysia before being sent to an unidentified third destination. Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, where the criminal case is ongoing.Links to Alice Huang and MegaspeedLi had reportedly been working with Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, for several years before the charges were filed.Chinese corporate registry records cited by the WSJ show that the couple established a cloud-computing joint venture, Century Longteng, in 2021.A social media photograph from January 2023, documenting Li's visit to a Shanghai-based AI equipment company, identified him as Century Longteng's chief strategy officer.Li, Alice Huang and Kang subsequently began building a network of partners in Southeast Asia to provide computing capacity to Chinese customers, according to people familiar with the business.They acquired the Singapore unit of a Chinese video game company and renamed it Megaspeed, with Alice Huang registered as a director.After telling Nvidia that Chinese technology giant Alibaba was an anchor customer, Megaspeed joined Nvidia's cloud partner programme in November 2023, the WSJ said, citing its earlier reporting. The partnership gave the company priority access to purchase the chipmaker's latest processors.Megaspeed brought servers to Malaysia and provided offshore computing capacity to Alibaba. However, some of those servers were allegedly sent to Shanghai-based technology company Century Litong in violation of US export controls, the newspaper reported.Century Longteng was a key shareholder in Century Litong until 2024, according to corporate registry records.Nvidia placed Megaspeed on an internal “no sell” list in June 2025, around the time the US and Singapore were investigating the company, the WSJ reported. Megaspeed has maintained that it “conducts legitimate and lawful business” and said Alice Huang left the company in August 2025.Singapore officials said they questioned Huang over suspicions of chip smuggling, allowed her to leave the country and barred her from re-entering.Megaspeed team linked to new ventureMegaspeed largely went dormant in Singapore after Huang's departure, but the team behind it is now running a new venture called Novagate Cloud, people familiar with the business told the newspaper.Established in 2025, Novagate describes itself as an Nvidia cloud partner and says it operates at least two data centres equipped with the company's advanced Blackwell chips.Shipment records reviewed by the WSJ show that Novagate received at least $300 million worth of hardware containing Nvidia chips at one of its entities in Malaysia during the first five months of 2026.The newspaper also identified corporate links between Novagate and companies associated with Century Litong.Novagate lists two Singaporeans as its director and company secretary. Both also hold the same positions at a company controlled by a director of a Singapore-based subsidiary linked to Century Litong. That director has recently been charged in Singapore with offences similar to those Li is accused of, the report said.A May report by short-selling firm Culper Research suggested Novagate was likely linked to Megaspeed, citing similarities between the companies' websites and the fact that one of Novagate's directors shared an address with Megaspeed's headquarters, it added.Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, where the criminal case is ongoing.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Tech services M&A deals rise 4.7% to 247 in Q3, value hits $5.3 billion: EY
articles.summary: EY reports tech services M&A rose 4.7% to 247 deals in Q3, with disclosed value at $5.3B, driven by data, enterprise apps and AI deployment capabilities.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Technology services mergers and acquisitions are increasingly focused on capabilities that can move artificial intelligence from experimentation to deployment in complex enterprise environments, with buyers prioritising data foundations, application expertise and AI-native services, according to an EY report.The EY Technology Services Deal Insights: Q3 CY26 round-up recorded 247 announced transactions during the quarter, up 4.7% from 236 in the June quarter. Disclosed deal value stood at about $5.3 billion. Four large transactions — Softcat-General Datatech, ITC Infotech-Happiest Minds, Bain Capital-Baudroie and CDW-Lovelytics — accounted for $2.8 billion of this value. Excluding these, disclosed deal value was about $2.5 billion, highlighting the concentration of deal value in a handful of large transactions.Data and AI deal activity rose 28% sequentially in Q3, as acquirers sought capabilities in advanced data engineering, modernisation, governance and AI-ready data infrastructure. The report said capabilities linked to Databricks were particularly prominent.Acquisition activity also extended across specialists in enterprise application platforms such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce and ServiceNow. These capabilities provide the process and workflow context needed to deploy AI across businesses. Deals in this segment included Accenture-McCoy & Partners and COMWARE, Argano-GoSaaS, NTT DATA-Netgain and Evidi-Datacon.Another emerging category is AI-native service providers, built around agentic delivery, reusable intellectual property, specialised engineering and forward-deployed implementation. The report cited the $53 million funding round for Hang Ten Systems, led by Mayfield and Xora Innovation, alongside Ode-Casper Studios and Norte Ventures-Asteras as examples of activity in this space.Strategic buyers are also using acquisitions to expand enterprise access and deepen domain expertise amid subdued organic growth and changes in traditional technology services delivery models. Transactions included ITC Infotech’s $643 million acquisition of Happiest Minds, Kyndryl’s $350 million acquisition of Healthcare IT Leaders, HCLTech’s acquisition of Guardian India Operations and TCS’s $369 million acquisition of MHP, the Porsche captive.“As enterprise AI moves into production, buyers are increasingly seeking the data foundations and application expertise needed to deliver measurable business outcomes. That shift is bringing greater scrutiny to AI-led revenues, proven use cases and reusable solutions,” said Shivani Nagpaul, partner, investment banking – technology, media and telecom, EY India.Private equity-backed consolidation gained ground, accounting for 41% of deal volume in Q3, compared with 36% in the first half of CY26. Direct private equity investments remained at 17%, while strategic buyers accounted for 42%, down from 47% in the first half of the year.Private equity investors remained selective, focusing on data, enterprise applications, cybersecurity and managed infrastructure businesses with clearer value-creation opportunities, recurring revenues and more predictable growth prospects.Money habits form by age 7.
